correctness.rationale: The square-zero lemma is proved from the kernel decomposition of a contraction and a constrained scalar optimization; the maximum is the top eigenvalue of a two-by-two symmetric matrix. The exact optimizing pair works for both endpoints. The diagonal-indexed upper-right block operator is norm-continuous by compact equicontinuity, has vanishing pairwise products, and retains the target supremum norm. The output coefficients have l1 mass at most the sharp square-zero q constant; norm-closed absolute convexity yields the upper inclusion. Single-coordinate optimizing pairs give the reverse inclusion, while complex phase rotation and balancedness cover all complex q. A stand-alone checker passed 35789 finite supplemental assertions; finite tests are not the proof.

value.rationale: An exact realization theorem across an entire parameter disk is a natural structural extension of the recent unimodular realization question. It applies to arbitrary compact absolutely convex subsets of an infinite-dimensional function space with one fixed pairwise-annihilating operator family, preserving the uniform norm and proving an exact parameter-dependent shape. The restriction to balance is natural at q=0, where every joint q=0 numerical range is rotation invariant. The theorem does not claim the known scalar rank-one coefficient as separately new.
